name: Thompson Park
season: Year-round (pool and splash pad are summer-only)
good_for_kids: Playground and splash pad right next to the zoo, plus paved paths that work fine with a stroller.
what_to_do: Olmsted-designed city park with a playground, splash pad, swimming pool, tennis courts, a golf course, walking trails, a bandstand, and Zoo New York on the grounds.

name: Zoo New York at Thompson Park
good_for_kids: Small enough to walk in an hour with toddlers; focuses on animals native to New York like black bears and wolves.
what_to_do: State zoo dedicated to species native to New York, including wolverines, black bears, eagles, mountain lions, Canada lynx and grey wolves, inside Thompson Park.

name: Bicentennial Park (Watertown)
good_for_kids: Another easy Black River stop downtown.
what_to_do: Riverside park along the Black River in downtown Watertown.

name: Marble Street Park
good_for_kids: Small downtown river park for a quick break.
what_to_do: Riverside park along the Black River with picnic space and scenic views.

name: Roswell P. Flower Memorial Library
good_for_kids: Redesigned children's room, preschool storytime and a summer reading club.
what_to_do: Public library with a children's department, preschool story programs, and a summer reading club for kids and teens.

name: Billy Beez
address: 21182 Salmon Run Mall Loop W, Suite A101, Watertown, NY 13601
good_for_kids: Slides, ball pit and bumper cars, plus a separate quieter toddler area (Mini Beez); good rainy or subzero-day option.
what_to_do: Indoor play center inside Salmon Run Mall with slides, bumper cars, a ball pit arena, arcade games and a toddler-only play area.

name: Carthage Park
good_for_kids: Large wooden playground (Kids' World), a skate park and marked woods trails; a splash pad and new playground are funded and planned but not yet built as of late 2026.
what_to_do: Village park with a recreation building, skate park, wooded walking trail system, and playground; new splash pad and playground construction is funded via a state grant.

name: Jack Williams Community Park
good_for_kids: The village's community park, used for the summer recreation program; closest public park to the Evans Mills/LeRay side of Fort Drum.
what_to_do: Village community park that hosts the Evans Mills summer recreation program.

name: Black River Trail
good_for_kids: Flat, paved former rail bed, fine for bikes and strollers; picnic area and river access at the Black River end.
what_to_do: 4.5-mile paved rail-trail for walking, biking, and cross-country skiing, with a picnic area and river access.

name: Sackets Harbor Battlefield State Historic Site
address: 504 W. Main Street, Sackets Harbor, NY 13685
season: Grounds open year-round at dark; visitor center/buildings open seasonally (May-Oct)
good_for_kids: Open lawns for running around, a National Recreation Trail, costumed-interpreter demonstrations, and a picnic area; kids 12 and under are free.
what_to_do: War of 1812 battlefield and naval yard site with a visitor center/museum, historic buildings, costumed interpreters, a picnic area, and walking trails.

name: Market Square Park
good_for_kids: Downtown village green, good stop while walking the historic district.
what_to_do: Village-run park in downtown Sackets Harbor.

name: Fort Pike Park
good_for_kids: Short walking loop around 1812-era earthworks with interpretive signs, a picnic table and an observation deck overlooking the harbor and Lake Ontario; good for older kids interested in history.
what_to_do: Village park built around the surviving War of 1812 earthworks of Fort Pike (originally Fort Volunteer), with a walking trail, interpretive signs, picnic table and observation deck.

name: Stoodley Park
good_for_kids: Small neighborhood village park; call the village office for current equipment.
what_to_do: Village-run park in Sackets Harbor.

name: Cerow Recreation Park
season: Year-round (ice arena Oct-early March; pool summer)
good_for_kids: Outdoor community pool in summer, plus tennis, basketball, ball fields and an ice arena in winter.
what_to_do: Town recreation complex with an outdoor community pool, walking trail, lighted tennis courts, basketball court, ball fields, and an ice arena (skating October-early March).

name: Antique Boat Museum
season: Seasonal (open for the 2026 season; call for exact dates)
good_for_kids: Large collection of boats to look at indoors and on the water; check ahead for kid programming.
what_to_do: Museum with the largest collection of antique and classic boats on display in North America, over 300 vessels.

name: Cape Vincent Recreation Park
good_for_kids: Tennis and basketball courts, ball fields and an ice rink in winter.
what_to_do: Town recreation park with tennis courts, basketball courts, an ice rink, baseball fields and a commercial kitchen/hall available for events.

name: Burnham Point State Park
season: Memorial Day weekend to Labor Day
good_for_kids: Small, quiet campground-style state park with a playground; good for a low-key picnic stop on the river.
what_to_do: Small St. Lawrence River state park with a playground, boat launch, fishing, camping and cabins.

name: Scenic View Park
good_for_kids: Lifeguarded sand beach, a pirate-ship-themed playground, and a boardwalk with an elevator instead of stairs down to the picnic area.
what_to_do: Village park on the St. Lawrence River with a seasonal swimming beach, playground, picnic pavilion, and a boardwalk with views of Boldt Castle.

name: Boldt Castle
good_for_kids: Big grounds and a real castle to explore; boat-only access via a shuttle, so budget time and a life jacket for little ones on the water.
what_to_do: Historic island castle and gardens in the St. Lawrence River, reachable only by boat/shuttle from Alexandria Bay; 2026 admission is $14 adult, $10 child (5-12).

name: Redwood Hill Preserve
good_for_kids: The Beatrice Rosamond Trail is a wheelchair/stroller-accessible all-access path to a lake overlook deck; a composting toilet is on site.
what_to_do: Nature preserve with 1.2 miles of easy trails including an ADA-accessible all-access trail to a Butterfield Lake overlook deck and trailside learning center.

name: Westcott Beach State Park
season: Camping mid-May-Columbus Day; 2026 swim season June 19-Sept 6
good_for_kids: Sandy Lake Ontario beach with a children's playground and camping right on site.
what_to_do: Lake Ontario state park with a sandy swimming beach, playground, boat launch, hiking trails, camping and cottages.

name: Wellesley Island State Park
good_for_kids: Swimming beach and playground plus the nature center next door; the largest camping complex in the Thousand Islands if you want to make a weekend of it.
what_to_do: Large St. Lawrence River state park with a swimming beach, playground, marina, golf course, camping, and the Minna Anthony Common Nature Center on site.

name: Minna Anthony Common Nature Center
season: May-Columbus Day (weekdays 9am-3pm, weekends 9am-6pm); limited off-season hours
good_for_kids: Nature trails and educational programs inside Wellesley Island State Park, plus seasonal canoe tours through Eel Bay.
what_to_do: Nature center inside Wellesley Island State Park with trails, exhibits, educational programs and seasonal canoe tours.

name: Cedar Point State Park
address: 36661 Cedar Point State Park Drive, Clayton, NY 13624
season: Early May-Columbus Day; 2026 swim season June 27-Sept 6
good_for_kids: Sandy beach and playground, one of the oldest state parks in the region.
what_to_do: St. Lawrence River state park with a sandy swimming beach, boat docks, fishing pier, playground and camping.

name: Kring Point State Park
good_for_kids: Playground on a peninsula with river/bay views; about half the campsites are waterfront.
what_to_do: St. Lawrence River peninsula state park with a playground, boat launch, camping, cabins and dockage.

name: Long Point State Park
address: 7495 State Park Road, Three Mile Bay, NY 13693
season: Early May-Labor Day; 2026 camping season May 15-Sept 6
good_for_kids: Playground on a protected bay, breezes help keep mosquitoes down.
what_to_do: Chaumont Bay state park with a playground, camping, cabins, boat launch and dockage.

name: Grass Point State Park
good_for_kids: Playground, playing fields and a swimming beach.
what_to_do: 114-acre St. Lawrence River state park in the Town of Orleans with a swimming beach, playground, playing fields, boat launch and camping.

name: Dewolf Point State Park
good_for_kids: Small, rustic island park; better for older kids into fishing/boating than for a playground visit (no playground on site).
what_to_do: Small 13-acre island state park on the St. Lawrence River with camping, a boat launch, fishing and a gazebo; no playground.

name: Remington Park
address: 11430 Pech River Road, Fort Drum, NY 13602
season: Beach/pond activities summer only, weather permitting; park grounds year-round
good_for_kids: Playgrounds, a beach with a lifeguard, and paddle boat/kayak rentals on Remington Pond; on-post, so bring installation access/ID.
what_to_do: Fort Drum's main recreation park on Remington Pond, with pavilions, playgrounds, volleyball, horseshoes, a fitness trail, and a summer swimming beach with paddle boat and kayak rentals.

name: Magrath Sports Complex & Pool
address: Tigris River Valley Road, BLDG 10050, Fort Drum, NY 13602
good_for_kids: Lifeguarded 25m pool with diving platforms; kids under 17 must pass a swim test for full pool use.
what_to_do: On-post MWR sports complex with a 25-meter indoor pool, basketball/volleyball courts, and an indoor track, open for family/open swim.

name: Lewis County Fairgrounds
season: Fair in summer; ice rink in winter (opens around Jan 6, weather permitting)
good_for_kids: Home of the Lewis County Fair; also has a winter ice rink with posted public hours.
what_to_do: County fairgrounds hosting the annual Lewis County Fair and a seasonal outdoor ice rink.

name: Whitaker Park
season: Mother's Day weekend through Columbus Day weekend
good_for_kids: Tent and RV camping park; good base for a family camping weekend.
what_to_do: Seasonal camping park with tent sites ($10/night) and RV sites ($15/night).

name: Whetstone Gulf State Park
season: Summer: Memorial Day-mid September; winter: Dec 15-March 15; 2026 swim season June 28-Sept 7 (beach weekends only from Aug 19)
good_for_kids: Man-made swimming area and playground at the campground; the gorge-rim trail is more of a hike for older kids.
what_to_do: 515-acre state park built around a 3-mile gorge on the Tug Hill Plateau, with a playground, swimming area, campground, hiking and cross-country ski trails.

name: Jefferson County Fairgrounds
good_for_kids: County fair with rides, animals and exhibits; classic summer outing.
what_to_do: Home of the annual Jefferson County Fair.

name: Southwick Beach State Park
season: Vehicle use fee charged in peak season
good_for_kids: A very long, wide dune beach that's shallow near shore, plus open playing fields for running around after swimming.
what_to_do: Swim at the guarded beach, play on the fields, and picnic among the dune grass.

name: Keewaydin State Park
season: Vehicle use fee charged in peak season
good_for_kids: A park with a swimming pool (not just river swimming) plus a marina where kids can watch St. Lawrence Seaway freighters go by.
what_to_do: Swim in the pool, watch ships from the marina, and picnic along the river.

name: Selkirk Shores State Park
season: Vehicle use fee charged in peak season (park states May 22-Sept 7 for the 2026 season)
good_for_kids: A supervised Lake Ontario beach plus a playground and easy woodland trails, a solid full-day option a bit further south.
what_to_do: Swim at the guarded beach, hike or bike the trails, and watch for migrating birds.

name: Salmon River Fish Hatchery
season: Visitor building open daily roughly April through November; outdoor viewing decks open until dusk
good_for_kids: Walk-through viewing decks over the fish ladder where kids can watch real salmon and trout up close, plus indoor displays on how the fish are raised.
what_to_do: Watch fish in the raceways and fish ladder, and read the displays on salmon and trout life stages.

name: Salmon River Falls Unique Area
address: Falls Road parking area off County Route 22, near Altmar
good_for_kids: A short, flat, stroller- and wheelchair-friendly packed-stone path (about a fifth of a mile) leads to railed overlooks of a 110-foot waterfall.
what_to_do: Walk the accessible trail to two railed overlook platforms of the falls.

name: Perch River Wildlife Management Area
address: accessed from State Route 12 and Allen, Buckminster, Vaadi, and Perch Lake roads
good_for_kids: Wide-open wetland and grassland good for a birdwatching walk; a plainer, less-developed area better suited to kids who are fine on unpaved roads and paths.
what_to_do: Walk the access roads and trails and look for waterfowl, eagles, and osprey.

name: Ashland Flats Wildlife Management Area
address: off Depot and Ashland roads, about 2 miles northeast of Three Mile Bay
good_for_kids: An accessible observation tower overlooking a wetland, an easy stop for younger kids to spot birds without a long walk.
what_to_do: Climb the observation tower and watch for wetland birds.

name: Lakeview Wildlife Management Area (South Sandy Creek Access)
good_for_kids: A wheelchair-accessible fishing pier on South Sandy Creek, an easy option for a family fishing stop.
what_to_do: Fish from the accessible pier or bank along South Sandy Creek.

name: French Creek Wildlife Management Area
address: via Crystal Springs Road (CR 4) to French Creek Road, about 4 miles from Clayton
good_for_kids: A calm creek with a hand launch, good for a first canoe or kayak trip with kids, plus meadow and woodland walking.
what_to_do: Paddle the creek from the hand launch or walk the meadow and woodland trails.

name: Otter Creek Preserve
good_for_kids: A wildlife-watching tower and a suspension bridge kids will enjoy crossing, on almost 2 miles of trail with a paved accessible section.
what_to_do: Cross the suspension bridge, climb the observation tower, and walk the creekside trail.

name: Zenda Farms Preserve
good_for_kids: An old farm property with three short loop trails, historic barns, community gardens, and boulders kids can climb on.
what_to_do: Walk one of three short loop trails past farm fields and historic buildings.

name: Baker Woods Preserve
good_for_kids: The biggest Indian River Lakes Conservancy trail network (over 10 miles across 16 connected trails), so families can pick a short loop or go longer; a pollinator garden blooms in spring.
what_to_do: Pick a loop from the trail network, visit the pollinator garden, or cross-country ski in winter.

name: Joseph A. Blake Wildlife Sanctuary
address: 31827 Middle Road, Watertown, NY (trailhead parking about 3 miles down Middle Road)
good_for_kids: 144 acres of connected trails close to Watertown with ponds to look for wildlife; there's a trail kiosk and a portable restroom at the parking area.
what_to_do: Hike or bike the trail network and watch for birds and wildlife around the ponds.

name: Carthage Free Library
good_for_kids: Storytime plus a therapy-dog reading program that suits preK through grade 6.
what_to_do: Small-town library with a summer reading program, family activities, and a Thursday therapy-dog reading session for early readers.

name: Hay Memorial Library
address: 105 South Broad Street, Sackets Harbor, NY 13685
good_for_kids: Kid's Korner and a Lego Club suit elementary-age kids; Teen Scene for older kids.
what_to_do: Village library with a kids' corner, a Lego club, take-and-make craft kits, and seasonal family programs.

name: Evans Mills Public Library
good_for_kids: Toddler story-and-craft time weekly, plus a 1000 Books Before Kindergarten early-literacy program.
what_to_do: Small library near Fort Drum's north gate serving the Evans Mills/Philadelphia area with toddler storytime and an early-literacy tracking program.

name: Lowville Free Library
good_for_kids: Weekly Tuesday storytime (Oct-May) plus a June-August summer reading program.
what_to_do: Lewis County's main library, with a regular storytime, Lego and craft activities, and a summer reading program for kids.

name: Adams Free Library
good_for_kids: Small rural library with a kids' book section, good for browsing with young readers.
what_to_do: Small village library in Adams (the 'Arbor Day Village') carrying a wide range of children's books; call ahead for current program schedule.

name: Hawn Memorial Library
good_for_kids: Themed summer programs (crafts, movies, story hour) that suit elementary-age kids.
what_to_do: Clayton's public library runs seasonal themed programming, a weekly story hour with a craft, and hands-on kids' activities most summer Saturdays.

name: Jefferson County Historical Society (Paddock Mansion)
good_for_kids: Grade-school kids enjoy the Victorian garden, pioneer cabin, and one-room schoolhouse outdoors; kids 5 and under free.
what_to_do: History museum in an 1870s mansion with 100,000+ local artifacts, an outdoor Victorian garden, pioneer cabin, and one-room schoolhouse.

name: 10th Mountain Division & Fort Drum Museum
address: Heritage Center, South Riva Ridge Loop, Fort Drum, NY 13602
good_for_kids: Military-history exhibits that suit school-age kids, especially those with a parent in the 10th Mountain Division.
what_to_do: On-post museum preserving the history of the 10th Mountain Division and Fort Drum, with group tours available on request.

name: Watertown Family YMCA Downtown Aquatic Center
good_for_kids: Recreation pool and splash pad suit toddlers; lap pool and swim lessons for older kids.
what_to_do: New $27.5M community and aquatic center downtown with an indoor recreation pool, lap pool, splash pad, and family swim lessons.

name: Dry Hill Ski Area
season: Winter, night skiing until 9pm weekdays/10pm weekends
good_for_kids: Beginner-friendly slopes and a snow-tubing park suit most kids; nursery/lessons available for young children.
what_to_do: Watertown's family ski, snowboard, and tubing hill since 1960, with 7 trails, night skiing, and a rental shop.

name: Snow Ridge Ski Resort
good_for_kids: 22 trails plus a tubing area and a nursery for ages 1-4 suit a range of kid ages.
what_to_do: Tug Hill ski resort averaging 230 inches of snow a year, with 22 trails, night skiing, glades, a terrain park, and tubing.

name: Thompson Park sledding hill
good_for_kids: A long-standing free sledding tradition ('The Hill') that suits most kid ages with adult supervision.
what_to_do: Historic city park with a well-known free sledding hill, plus an outdoor skating area, in winter.

name: Seaway Lanes
good_for_kids: Junior pricing (16 and under) and family-bowling nights suit most ages.
what_to_do: 30-lane bowling alley with a bar and cafe, junior and military discounts, and family-themed bowling nights.

name: Watertown Municipal Arena (Northern Credit Union Community Arena)
address: 600 William T Field Dr, Watertown, NY 13601
good_for_kids: Toddler-to-adult skate rentals and a learn-to-skate program suit beginners.
what_to_do: Municipal ice rink with daily public skating in winter, a learn-to-skate program, and family skate nights with music.

name: Little Theatre of Watertown
good_for_kids: Family-friendly shows suit school-age kids and up; check each show's content before bringing younger kids.
what_to_do: North Country's longest-running community theater (est. 1931), staging family-friendly productions, often at the Strand Theatre in Watertown.

name: Clayton Opera House
good_for_kids: Children's theater shows and a summer theater program for ages 5-16.
what_to_do: Historic 1903 riverside theater hosting children's theater, family movies, and a summer theater program for kids.

name: Carthage Village Park (Kids' World & Riders Edge Skate Park)
good_for_kids: Kids' World wooden playground suits younger kids; the skate park suits older kids on boards or scooters.
what_to_do: Village park with a large wooden playground (Kids' World), the Riders Edge skate park, ball fields, and walking trails.

name: Pine Plains Bowling Center
address: Conway Road, BLDG 4320, Fort Drum, NY 13602
good_for_kids: HyperBowling interactive lanes and a snack bar suit a family outing.
what_to_do: On-post bowling center with interactive HyperBowling lanes, a snack bar, and birthday-party bookings.

name: Robert C. McEwen Library
address: Camp Hale Road, BLDG 4300, Fort Drum, NY 13602
good_for_kids: Dedicated children's library area within an 18,000 sq ft facility.
what_to_do: On-post MWR library with a dedicated children's library section, multimedia area, and story/event programming.

name: Fort Drum Youth Center
address: Chapel Drive, BLDG 10788, Fort Drum, NY 13602
good_for_kids: Free membership for grades 6-12; computer labs, art rooms, and dance classes after school.
what_to_do: Free after-school and weekend center for middle- and high-school-age military kids, with sports, clubs, and special events.

name: Outdoor Recreation / Gear to Go
address: Iraqi Freedom Drive, BLDG 11115, Fort Drum, NY 13602
good_for_kids: Family gear rentals (snowshoes, sleds, bikes, boats) support outdoor outings with kids of any age.
what_to_do: On-post equipment rental counter for winter gear (skis, snowshoes, snowboards) and summer gear (boats, bikes, camping equipment).
